chunks: And from him, from Ali, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Khas'ami, who said:

Hafs al-Kunasasi asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) while I was with him - regarding the saying of Allah, Exalted and Mighty: 'And to Allah is due the pilgrimage of the house for whoever is able to find a way to it.' What does He mean by that? He said: 'Whoever is sound in his body, his path is clear to him, he has provisions and a mount, then he is among those who can perform the pilgrimage.' Or he said: 'Among those who have wealth.'

Hafs al-Kunasasi said to him: 'And if he is sound in his body, his path is clear to him, he has provisions and a mount, and he did not perform the pilgrimage, is he among those who can perform the pilgrimage?' He said: 'Yes.'

key_terms.مَنِ اسْتَطَاعَ إِلَيْهِ سَبِيلًا: Whoever is able to find a way to it

ai.seo_question: What are the specific conditions that define 'ability' (istita'ah) for the obligation of Hajj in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elucidates the practical dimensions of 'istita'ah' (ability) by specifying physical health, security of the path, provisions, and transport as the criteria for Hajj's obligation. The dialogue with Hafs al-Kunasī confirms that the obligation is immediate and binding upon the possession of these conditions, a view central to Shia jurisprudence regarding the timing of the Hajj duty. This definition underscores the balance between spiritual intent and material capacity in fulfilling the fifth pillar of Islam.
